title: Infinite cardinal arithmetic: sums, products, and powers
summary: Infinite sums and products can preserve size, while power sets always make it larger.
abstract: An infinite set can have the same size as a collection of pairs of its elements. Assuming the axiom of choice, this holds for every infinite set and explains why sums and nonzero products of infinite sizes equal the larger size. Collections of functions behave differently. The real numbers have the size of all subsets of the natural numbers, and taking all subsets of any set always produces a strictly larger size. Infinite cardinal arithmetic makes these differences precise.
